A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCP-∆r defense. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite the expanded title and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original extraction attacks, utility measurements, fine-tuning experiments, and synthetic simulations in Table 2, Figures 1–5, and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds MMLU and IFEval utility experiments in Appendix D.7 and Table 7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, relative-probability aggregation, token-selection score, base-model smoothing, and both SCP-∆r variants are unchanged. Expanded explanations and downstream testing do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.7 adds MMLU question-answering and IFEval instruction-compliance evaluation. This substantially broadens utility coverage beyond next-token prediction on the retained MathAbstracts, StoryTelling, and CodeInstructions datasets. Names2IDs and all existing extraction scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding extraction comparisons retain No CP, CP-∆, CP-∆KL, CP-Fuse, CP-∆r, and the same SCP-∆r variants. Newly cited membership-inference attacks are discussed but not evaluated. Table 7 provides a component ablation without introducing a new competing defense.

E3.justification: v2 adds five-shot MMLU accuracy on Llama-2-7b and IFEval prompt-level accuracy on Llama-2-7b-chat, comparing smoothing at m = 10 against no smoothing. Section 5.4 also introduces normalized attack score aggregation. Existing extraction protocols, training budgets, splits, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.7 adds a controlled with-versus-without-smoothing analysis of downstream utility. Existing smoothing-level, memorization-level, raw-probability aggregation, synthetic-bound, canary-repetition, and LoRA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 16-seed SpaRPS analysis, 200-trial synthetic analysis with standard deviations and significance reporting, five-trial LoRA evaluation, and Table 2 standard errors. The added utility results introduce no new uncertainty estimates or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds MMLU scores of 45.83% without smoothing and 45.75% with smoothing, and IFEval scores of 31.42% and 31.61%, respectively. Table 2 adds NAS values, including 0.11 for SCP-∆r-b and 0.22 for CP-∆r. Existing scores and plots are unchanged; the Figure 1 discussion changes the quoted coverage from 95% to 90% for B approximately 2.1 at m = 1024.

T1.justification: The SpaRPS definitions, protection and utility bounds, and all proofs in Appendices A–B remain unchanged. The limited mathematical addition is the NAS definition in Section 5.4: normalize attack scores to [0,1] and average them with TTE contributions weighted by 1/3.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims remain: smoothing and relative probabilities provide tighter extraction bounds and stronger empirical protection while preserving utility. v2 separates the NAF-to-TDE connection into its own contribution bullet, but v1 already claimed that this connection was previously unstudied and established it.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly presents SpaRPS as an idealization requiring enforcement and distinguishes the behavioral conjecture from observed probability shifts. Sections 5–6 add discussion of attacks outperforming LiRA under restricted conditions, unresolved optimality assumptions, and near-duplicate partitioning limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-repository link and specifies model variants, five-shot MMLU evaluation, and the smoothing setting for the new utility tests. Existing hardware, preprocessing instructions, and regular and LoRA training parameters are retained. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fu et al. (2023) and Zhang et al. (2025a, Min-k%++) to contextualize LiRA limitations, plus Hendrycks et al. (2021) and Zhou et al. (2023) for the new benchmarks. The central positioning relative to NAF methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises parts of the introduction, SpaRPS motivation, results discussion, and limitations, and adds a dedicated Utility Evaluation subsection and Appendix D.7. It expands the title and changes author ordering and affiliation presentation. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a NAS column and Table 7 is added. All five figures retain identical plotted content, while figures, Algorithm 1, and surrounding text are repositioned through reflow. The title block, running headers, and conference footer also change.

improvement.justification: The new MMLU and IFEval comparisons strengthen utility-preservation evidence beyond v1's next-token measurements. The code pointer and clearer discussion of theoretical assumptions also improve usability and interpretation. The gain is limited because the downstream tests are briefly specified and report only point estimates; the underlying method and extraction evidence remain unchanged.
